summary: Cheap, row-readable restack. The align swap partly undoes the landed parallel align at turn_4, and the pre-norm half reuses an already-checked kernel. One real gap to fix before building: SGLang's 32-expert align does NOT give local-only blocks (remote routes go into -1 blocks), so prepare must time the align together with the Marlin pair and the sorted silu, not the align alone.
justification: The mechanism holds up. _align_parallel_kernel runs 33 CTAs on 132 SMs, and each one streams all n = 8T route ids twice in 512-id chunks, so its cost grows linearly with T: 16.7 us at T=753, 68.3 us at T=3012, 394 us at T=16384. SGLang's moe_align_block_size over 32 experts costs 139 us at T=16384, which scales linearly to about 25 us at T=3012, matching the pre-port master's ~27 us. That makes about -40 us at turn_4 plausible. The pre-norm numbers (24.8 -> 20.1 us at T=3012, 13.0 -> 9.7 at T=753) come from moe-pre-post-norm-triton-multitoken's own prepare A/B, which passed correctness, and the -45 us turn_4 estimate is consistent (~1.4% of 3319 us sliding, ~0.9% of 4849 us full). The headline effect, about +0.3-0.5%, sits well inside the ~±1.5% CI. The Marlin rows move ±70 us between identical-code runs (turn_4 sliding: 2093 / 2118 / 2148 / 2223 us across four recent runs), so the result can only be read on the align and pre-norm kernel rows and the prepare logs, as the hypothesis says. WEAKEST LINK: the change says 'keeping local-routes-only blocks', but moe_align_block_size(local_ids, bsm, 32) puts the ~7/8 remote routes into -1 blocks (moe-align-32-experts-first-turn's md says so explicitly). At T=3012 with bsm 64 that is roughly 330 extra -1 m-blocks next to ~80 local ones. Marlin (is_ep) and _silu_mul_sorted then walk a list about 5x longer up to n_padded. The archive suggests Marlin does not care: turn_4 Marlin was 2093/2173 us before the local-only port and 2148/2115 us after, which is within noise. But a prepare gate that times only the align could pick an align that is faster on its own and slower end to end. Gate on the whole _experts_marlin call (align + w13 Marlin + silu + w2 Marlin) in the graph with a cold-L2 flush at T=753 and T=3012, and switch it ON only when the end-to-end time drops by more than the timing noise. Also, 'bit-exact' needs care: Marlin output per route is order-independent with use_atomic_add=False, so bit-exact is a fair expectation. Compare only local rows, since remote cache3 rows are unwritten or garbage in both versions.
confounders: stack-tonight-five-prefill (landed moe-align-local-routes-parallel-port inside it): this hypothesis partly reverts that sub-change at T > 1024, so any turn_4 align gain is that port's own T-scaling being undone. It is still attributable, because the align kernel rows (_align_parallel_kernel vs moe_align/count_and_sort) appear in the profile and prepare logs both timings.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (landed silu-mul-triton-local-rows-marlin-turn inside it): _silu_mul_sorted consumes the align's sorted_ids/n_padded. With SGLang's layout it walks the -1 blocks too (masked, so correctness is unaffected but there is extra work), so the silu row may grow slightly at turn_4 and offset some of the align saving. Time it inside the end-to-end gate.

experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: it fixes MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS = 4096, which decides that turn_4 (T=3012) is on the Marlin path where this align change applies. If that threshold changes, for example because a queued turn_4 rewrite lands, the align half becomes dead code at turn_4. No confound for this run.

sglang-pipeline-parity: the pre-norm replaces state['pre_expert_norm'] (MuseSpark1xRMSNorm) from the parity pipeline. The Triton kernel uses the module's _get_effective_weight(), so it does not depend on how parity built the module. No confound.
interference: No companions. Each of the two sub-changes affects disjoint kernels with their own profile rows (align vs the pre-expert RMSNorm), and each logs an in-prepare A/B per T class (CUDA graph, cold L2). The two halves are already separable from a single run without a control. Reverting stack-tonight-five's align port (ab-revert) would only reproduce what this hypothesis does at T > 1024. An ab-tune of the gate threshold is not worth a check while prefill has 8 checks left. Make the result unambiguous by changing the prepare gate, not by adding a companion: gate the align on end-to-end _experts_marlin time and print both the align-only and the end-to-end numbers.
rules_flags: Pre-norm weight precision: the archived patch stores state['pre_w_eff'] = (1 + w) as fp32. TASK.md says BF16 weights stay BF16 'or smaller, losslessly'. The archived run passed with checks.flagged empty, so the risk is low. Still, keep the effective weight in the dtype _get_effective_weight() returns, or load the bf16 w and add 1 in-kernel in fp32, rather than storing a widened copy.

Prepare-time gating by timing: fine as long as the choice is keyed only by T class (shape) and timed on synthetic routing, never on data. Keep the align fallback decision static per class, with no branching on n_padded or other device values inside kernel_fn.
The extended _align_par_setup check uses .cpu() and prints. Those are fine in prepare(); make sure none of it leaks into the _experts_marlin hot path.
open_questions: Does sgl_kernel's moe_align_block_size at Marlin's small block sizes (bsm 16-64) put the -1 bucket last? If so, a one-thread fix-up of n_padded to the local total, at about 2 us, would restore local-only blocks for Marlin and silu and remove the weakest link entirely.

Is the ~25 us SGLang 32-expert align at T=3012 measured or extrapolated? The cited ~17+10 us figure was for the 256-expert call. The prepare log line will answer this, so record it in the attempt file.

At T=753 _align_parallel is 16.7 us, and SGLang's two-kernel align is probably ~8-12 us there, close to the 0.9x gate. Expect turn_1 align to stay on _align_parallel, which makes turn_1's expected gain pre-norm only (~3 us).
